note: Competitor angle only — refuting where a thinner rival (CLI confirm + open plan files, or a talk-first thin loop on existing propose/confirm) would beat this spine-first master plan on North-Star outcomes. Severity only where the finding still traces to a North-Star criterion.

findings.criterion: A project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD
findings.message: The North Star’s product is the talk path, not the ledger. This draft invents a nine-phase inversion that deliberately ships load-bearing storage, tokens, supervisor, and a zero-spend stub before any durable “describe → Face → propose → confirm → run” surface John can use. A competitor that reuses the already-cited proposeCommission/confirmCommission halves and one real Crucible path would deliver the NS experience while this plan is still grepping start-paths and proving WAL concurrency. Spine-first is a build aesthetic; competitor-first would put one continuous talk→confirm→execute loop green early and harden under it. As written, the plan optimizes for not being embarrassed by a second writer, not for not being beaten by a thinner steward that already talks.

findings.section: Success criteria; Phase 4 rehearsal; Phase 5 HALT-first; Phase 10 acceptance
findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step; only on explicit confirmation Anchor executes a real trio run; plan returns as a reviewable artifact; Roadmap shows truth
findings.message: Success criteria 1–5 are an end-to-end competitive product. The phases never define a single early “thin competitive slice” that hits all of them on outcomes before the full spine is complete. Phase 4’s rehearsal is explicitly a trio STUB with zero spend; Phase 5 is the first real Crucible cycle; artifact/talk refine and full auth-ON outcomes wait until 7–9/10. A rival product ships one ugly-but-real loop (named step, confirm who, real run, plan on screen, status not lying) and iterates. This plan’s first “real” moments are fragmented across late phases, so there is no early falsification of the whole NS story—only of subsystems competitors may not need to win the demo.

findings.section: Phase 4 (rehearsal commission); Phase 5 (real Crucible); Phase 10 (auth-ON outcomes)
findings.criterion: Anchor executes the confirmed commission as a real trio run; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: The draft makes a continuous stub path the CI backbone “from this phase onward,” while the real HALT→ask→confirm→resume cycle is a later special proof. Competitors who dogfood the production engine early discover resume lossiness, gate text drift, and status lies under real load. A suite that stays green on a no-spend stub while real Crucible is a single observed cycle in Phase 5 is exactly how you ship “works in CI, fails when John talks to a live steward.” Real trio is the competitive bar for criterion 3/5; the plan structurally treats it as the expensive special case after the fake path is institutionalized.

findings.criterion: real execution + validated handback (usable plan artifact after a real trio run); no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime (non-goal tension)
findings.message: D-A locks adapter-side extraction and treats absent uncertainty_flags/human_wait as REFUSAL, while forbidding trio changes. An integrated competitor that owns (or patches) the engines will emit clean structured handbacks and always show a plan. This design will systematically refuse runs that “worked” in Crucible but did not emit extractable fields—so John paid for a commission and gets no absorbed artifact, only a refusal. That is a competitive loss on “the produced plan comes back as an artifact,” not a durability win. Either the non-goal must be reopened for minimal native fields, or the plan must define a degraded-but-reviewable path (raw blob + partial card) that still satisfies “read on screen” without inventing fields. As written, integrity-by-refusal hands the usable outcome to the rival who integrated.

findings.section: Phase 1 classifyArtifact falsify; Phase 8 artifact card / DOC-TRIO MANIFEST
findings.criterion: the produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read on screen and change by talking; no bespoke plan template (Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.message: Competitors win “read the plan” by opening the markdown the engines already wrote. This plan bets Phase 1/8 on classifyArtifact/buildArtifactCard and, if that fails, a DOC-TRIO MANIFEST “packaging” layer. Packaging that is not a “new template” can still be a second presentation shape John must learn while the real doc-trio sits on disk. If the falsification fails and option (a) becomes the path, the competitive experience is “artifact card of a manifest of a plan,” not “the Crucible plan on screen.” That drifts toward the non-goal edge (bespoke presentation) while losing to the rival who simply surfaces the files. The plan needs a hard preference: fail open to the native doc-trio paths as the primary read surface; classifier/manifest is secondary chrome, never the gate on readability.

findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; John describes in his own words; change by talking
findings.message: Industry competitors treat the dialogue itself as durable memory. This plan makes ZERO chat turns persisted a hard success criterion and replaces it with structured draft-Face state. That may satisfy E5 ledger purity, but it is a competitive risk on the feeling of talking: after reconnect, rivals restore the conversation; this restores a compiled draft and “keep going.” If the draft schema loses nuance John spoke, the steward cannot truly “compile that description”—it compiles a thinning of it. The plan never proves that structured draft fidelity is competitive with transcript retention for the NS verbs (describe, correct, confirm). Without an acceptance test that a multi-turn framing reconnect preserves every locked commitment John uttered (not merely byte-identical draft bytes), rivals win the core UX while this plan wins an internal ledger aesthetic.

findings.section: Phase 5 (gate answer IS a micro-commission); Phase 7 confirm surface
findings.criterion: nothing is spent, written, or started without human confirmation; plan/change by talking; Crucible’s multi-gate path is the normal path
findings.message: Confirmation is required; full commission ceremony (skill + seat + depth + ceiling + disk impact + step echo) on every gate answer is not. Crucible has three approval gates by design; a competitor that still records who/when/what with a one-screen “Approve Stage-1 Master Plan?” will complete the same human-in-the-loop law with far less friction. Routing every gate through the same propose→confirm surface as a paid commission risks confirmation fatigue and wrong-clicking under load—exactly when the draft says HALT is the normal path. The plan should distinguish spend-confirm (new trio work, budget) from gate-confirm (advance existing run) while keeping one ledger/who/idempotency spine. As written, ceremony parity is purity theater that a thinner rival will out-UX on the path John hits most.

findings.topic: confirm surface density vs clear spend decision
findings.section: Phase 7 confirm surface as primary deliverable
findings.criterion: proposes a commission for a named roadmap step showing what runs before any spend; only on explicit confirmation
findings.message: Criterion 2 is “John knows what he is approving.” Competitors often win with a sparse confirm. This phase piles bound step, skill/seat/depth, hard ceiling, disk impact, size-class re-confirm, proposal diffs, and grasscatcher into one screen and makes answering four questions the GREEN bar. Over-dense confirms are a known competitive failure mode: people approve without reading, or refuse good work because the prompt feels like a contract. The plan has no inclusion test that every field on the confirm screen is necessary for the spend decision versus audit detail that belongs post-confirm in the ledger. Without ruthless prioritization (step + skill/seat/depth + ceiling first; everything else secondary), the “primary deliverable” becomes the rival’s easy “Start?” button in disguise—or worse, a wall John clicks through, breaking the spirit of explicit confirmation.

findings.topic: local-only ledger vs visible campaign truth
findings.section: Phase 1 D-B; Phase 2 ledger spine; Phase 9 honest Roadmap; deferred export
findings.criterion: the campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; when work runs, the Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: “Single source of truth” that lives only under %LOCALAPPDATA% and treats synced paths as poison is durable engineering, but a competitor whose project board is where John already looks (synced folder, always-open UI, multi-session) will own “what is running?” in practice. Export is deferred; mobile is non-goal; AWAITING YOU is in-app only. If the authoritative Roadmap is invisible whenever Anchor is not the focused machine-local app, the ledger is a single source of truth nobody consults—and the rival’s weaker but visible status wins. The plan must either ship a read-only derived export early enough that “Roadmap shows the truth” is true in John’s actual attention surface, or explicitly accept that SSOT is Anchor-process-local and weaken the honest-status claim accordingly. Right now it claims campaign-ledger truth while building a vault competitors can out-visibility.

findings.criterion: driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; spoken description / spoken correction (success criteria language)
findings.message: The draft’s own success criteria say “spoken description” and “spoken correction,” then D-D amends talking to typed dialogue and parks speech-to-text. Competitors ship voice as table stakes on “talk to your agent.” If John’s North Star language (“talking,” “spoken”) meant voice, this amendment silently cedes the literal differentiator to rivals while keeping the metaphor in the copy. Either the North Star and success criteria must be rewritten to “typed conversational dialogue” before Stage-1 lock (so acceptance cannot demand speech), or speech cannot be a casual non-goal tack-on. Competitor pressure: do not market talk and ship type without an explicit, recorded NS rewrite—otherwise acceptance will fight the amendment, or the product will feel like a downgrade next to voice-native agents.

findings.section: Phase 4 NEVER-AUTO-RETRY; lost → re-commission; Phase 9 park/restart/kill
findings.criterion: nothing spent/started without human confirmation; Roadmap shows truth across park/restart/kill
findings.message: Honest `lost` and no silent spend are correct under the confirmation law. Competitors still win daily trust by reattaching a live session after browser blip or UI restart without a full re-propose ceremony. The draft tests detachment well but offers only re-commission after lease expiry—no first-class “reattach still-running work you already confirmed” path distinct from “spend again.” If lease expiry is aggressive (“tens of seconds”) and reattach is slow, John will face re-confirm loops rivals avoid, while still having paid for the original commission. The competitive fix that still honors NS: reattach without new spend when the same confirmation token/run is still live; require fresh confirm only when a new process would start or budget would extend. As written, liveness purity can become confirmation spam that trains John to prefer a competitor’s sticky session.

findings.topic: compile brightness vs useful roadmap rival
findings.section: Phase 1 D-C; Phase 6 compile lint / commissionability
findings.criterion: steward compiles description into Face and Campaign Roadmap and proposes commission for a named step — without the steward doing the planning itself
findings.message: D-C’s WHAT/WHY-only steps correctly protect the non-goal “steward does not plan.” Competitors’ roadmaps often include just enough HOW to make “what do I commission next?” obvious. Strict lint plus “split or mark non-commissionable” can yield a Face that is pure but hard to drive—steps too vague to bind skill/seat/depth confidently, forcing disambiguation loops Phase 7 already fears. The competitive risk is a beautiful non-planning roadmap that loses to a slightly more operational one. The plan should require that every commissioned step is not only non-HOW but also specifically proposable (skill + seat + depth fillable without inventing plan content)—a positive commissionability bar, not only a negative HOW ban—so compile serves drive-by-talk, not purity.

findings.topic: pre-answer deferral vs gate-chatty rival experience
findings.section: Phase 1 deferred pre-answer; Phase 5; Phase 10 pre-answering static gates
findings.criterion: driven by talking; nothing auto-started without confirmation; Crucible gates remain human
findings.message: Deferring static pre-answer until after the resume channel is proven is safety-sound and NS-aligned for the three Crucible approvals. Competitors will still feel snappier on non-approval static halts during the long build. This is not a call to pre-answer approvals; it is a competitive note that Phase 5+ real runs will be chattier than necessary until Phase 10, training John on a worse product than the end state. Mitigate by allowing a narrow, inventory-hash-exact pre-answer for non-approval static gates as soon as Phase 5 is green—not only after full auth-ON sweep—so the normal HALT path is not artificially worse than the rival for months of dogfooding.

findings.topic: phase numbering vs competitor onboarding clarity
findings.message: Dual numbering (Phase N — Phase N-1) is an internal accounting mess that would never survive a competitor’s one-pager. It does not itself break the North Star, but it will slow Stage-2 decomposition and cross-shark reference. Rename to a single sequence before lock so the plan can be attacked and built without a translation layer.
